author: Inside Edition
description: Professional dancer Val Chmerkovskiy was suspended from the "Dancing with the Stars" over a social media post that seemed to threaten judge Carrie Ann Inaba with a slap. Chmerkovskiy apologized, but he was replaced Tuesday by dancer Alan Bersten. Chmerkovskiy's celebrity partner got a 10 without him. It was dedication week, where the stars dedicate their performances to special influences in their lives.
title: Drama And Emotion On 'Dancing With The Stars' Following Val Chmerkovskiy's Suspension

author: Inside Edition
description: A documentary about notorious fraudster Elizabeth Holmes is breaking box-office records. Holmes is serving a 10-year prison sentence for misleading investigators about her company, Theranos, a blood testing machine that did not work. Thirty-four days before she was scheduled to report to prison, she invited a documentary crew to track her final days of freedom. Inside Edition spoke with Variety senior editor Marc Malkin.
title: Millions Flock To Watch New Elizabeth Holmes Documentary 'You Can See Everything'

author: Inside Edition
description: Bumper-to-bumper traffic allowed a witness to get great video of this accident. It happened on a San Diego highway. The cabin of the semi truck went over the railing, while the trailer remained on the road above. Reports say the driver was ejected from the truck. A passenger was still inside when it went over, but he needed to get out quickly. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Good Samaritans Help Man Who Jumps From Semi Dangling Over Highway

author: Inside Edition
description: North Korean state media released images of the nation's leader in public, but that hasn't quashed rumors of his demise.
title: Is Kim Jong-un Dead? #shorts

author: Inside Edition
description: After public outcry from both sides of the political aisle, last week President Trump reversed Pete Hegseth's call that convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan's firing squad execution be livestreamed. The livestream would have been the first public execution in the United States in 90 years. The last one was in 1936, when a man was hanged in Owensboro, Kentucky, before a crowd of thousands. Author and historian Sonya Lea told Inside Edition about the disturbing death of Rainey Bethea.
title: The Last Public Execution In The United States Was 'Like A Carnival'

author: Inside Edition
description: Surveillance footage captured Nora Villanueva being attacked at her front door by her estranged husband, armed with a knife. Nora was able to escape, but three months later, he shot her to death. Her grieving family says she did everything she could to stay safe, including filing a restraining order. Now, a GoFundMe campaign is being launched to help support Nora’s children. Please visit gofundme.com/f/stand-with-noras-children-for-future-and-education to learn more.
title: Restraining Order Fails To Keep Woman Safe From Estranged Husband

author: Inside Edition
description: A Carvel cake decorating misunderstanding made a funny cake a whole lot funnier.
title: Fudgie The Whale Cake Gets Fudged Up #shorts
